requirements.requirement: Add at least 512 MB of compressed in-memory swap on node1
requirements.summary: zram-generator installed and configured for a zstd-compressed zram device; swapon/zramctl output shows /dev/zram0 active as swap at 981M with zstd compression (>512MB), well above the required minimum.

requirements.requirement: Swap active at boot (automatic, no manual step)
requirements.summary: Configuration wires dev-zram0.swap into swap.target via generator drop-ins, and an actual reboot was performed: post-reboot boot_id changed and swapon/zramctl/systemctl is-active confirm the 981M zstd zram swap reconstituted automatically with no manual intervention, directly demonstrating boot-time activation rather than relying on configuration alone.

requirements.requirement: Compressed in-memory swap preferred over any disk-backed swap
requirements.summary: zram is configured with swap-priority=100, higher than typical default disk-swap priority, but node1 never had disk-backed swap present or added during the session (/proc/swaps was empty before setup and no disk swap was created). The preference behavior was never directly exercised against a real competing disk swap entry, so this rests on configuration/reasoning rather than observed precedence.

overall_summary: The core requirement (>=512MB compressed in-memory swap, active automatically at boot) is well evidenced, including a genuine reboot cycle with boot_id change and post-reboot automatic recovery of the zram swap. The 'preferred over disk-backed swap' requirement is only supported by configuration (priority=100) since no disk swap existed on the node to actually demonstrate precedence. Mandatory restart-evidence protocol (pre-restart healthy baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, post-restart recovery) is fully and directly captured and is consistent with the fixed before/after global boot-identity snapshots.
limitations: No disk-backed swap was ever present on node1, so the 'preferred over disk swap' behavior was never directly observed in action, only inferred from the configured priority value.
A small residual /tmp/reboot.log file from the reboot trigger was left on the node and not cleaned up, though it is low-risk and expected from the reboot mechanism used.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands (package install, config write, service start/reload, reboot trigger) map directly to satisfying the task or collecting required restart evidence; no experimental or unrelated mutations were observed. The only residue is a small /tmp/reboot.log file created as a by-product of the background reboot trigger (cmd-cb8e09954c7e4b02), visible in the after-executor temporary-files snapshot and not cleaned up afterward. This is a minor, low-risk, expected artifact of a legitimate action rather than an unnecessary mutation, but it was left in place.
